**Australia**, officially the **Commonwealth of Australia**, is a country comprising the [mainland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainland_Australia) of the [Australian continent](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_(continent)>), the island of [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania) and [numerous smaller islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Australia).<sup>[\[N 6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-22)</sup> It has a land area of 7,688,287 km<sup>2</sup> (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the [sixth-largest country in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area), and is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent. It is a [megadiverse country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megadiverse_countries), and its size gives it a wide variety of landscapes and [climates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_Australia), including large [deserts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deserts_of_Australia) centrally and [tropical rainforests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forests_of_Australia) along the coast.

The ancestors of [Aboriginal Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians) began arriving from [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia) 50,000 to 65,000 years ago, during the [Last Glacial Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Glacial_Period). By the time of British settlement, Aboriginal Australians spoke more than 250 distinct languages and had one of the oldest living cultures in the world.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Flood_2019-2-23)[Australia's written history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Australia) commenced with [Dutch exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_maritime_exploration_of_Australia) of most of the coastline in the 17th century. British colonisation began in 1788 with the establishment of the penal [colony of New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_New_South_Wales). By the mid-19th century, most of the continent had been explored by European settlers and five additional self-governing [British colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_colony) were established, each gaining [responsible government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsible_government) by 1890. The [colonies federated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia) in 1901, forming the Commonwealth of Australia. This continued a process of increasing autonomy from the United Kingdom, highlighted by the *[Statute of Westminster Adoption Act 1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute_of_Westminster_Adoption_Act_1942)*, and culminating in the *[Australia Act 1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Act_1986)*.

Australia is a [parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_democracy) with a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy), and a [federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation) comprising [six states and ten territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_Australia). Its population of almost 29 million is highly urbanised and heavily concentrated on the eastern seaboard.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Australian_Bureau_of_Statistics-2023-24)[Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra) is the nation's capital, while [its most populous cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Australia_by_population) are [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney) and [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne), each with a population of more than five million. [Australia's culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Australia) is diverse, and the country has one of the [highest foreign-born populations in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_immigrant_and_emigrant_population). It has a highly [developed economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developed_economy) and one of the [highest per capita incomes globally](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GNI_(PPP)_per_capita>). Its abundant natural resources and well-developed [international trade relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_largest_trading_partners_of_Australia) are crucial to [the country's economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Australia). It [ranks highly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_rankings_of_Australia) for quality of life, [health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_in_Australia), [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_Australia), economic freedom, civil liberties and political rights.

Australia is a [middle power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_power), and has the world's [fourteenth-highest military expenditure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_military_expenditures). It is a member of international groups including: the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations), the [G20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G20), the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD), the [World Trade Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization), [Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific_Economic_Cooperation), the [Pacific Islands Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islands_Forum), the [Pacific Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Community) and the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations). Australia also participates in the defence, intelligence and security alliances [ANZUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANZUS), [AUKUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AUKUS) and [Five Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Eyes). It is a [major non-NATO ally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_non-NATO_ally) of the United States.

## Etymology

The name *Australia* (pronounced [//](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English) in [Australian English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_English))<sup>[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-25)</sup> is derived from the Latin *[Terra Australis Incognita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_Australis_Incognita)* ('unknown southern land'), a name used for a hypothetical continent in the Southern Hemisphere since ancient times.<sup>[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-National_Library_of_Australia-2024-26)</sup> Several 16th-century cartographers used the word *Australia* on maps, but not to identify modern Australia.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-27)

When the Dutch began visiting and mapping Australia in the 17th century, they called the continent [*New Holland*](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Holland_(Australia)>). The name *Australia* was popularised by the explorer [Matthew Flinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Flinders), who circumnavigated the continent in 1803. However, when his account of his voyage was published in 1814, the name *Terra Australis* was used.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-National_Library_of_Australia-2024-26)

Governor of New South Wales [Lachlan Macquarie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lachlan_Macquarie) officially recommended the name *Australia* to replace *New Holland* in December 1817. The [British Admiralty](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiralty_(United_Kingdom)>) adopted the name in 1824, and the [British Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_the_United_Kingdom) used it in legislation in 1828.<sup>[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-National_Library_of_Australia-2024-26)</sup> The United Kingdom [Hydrographic Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_Hydrographic_Office) used the new name in *The Australia Directory* of 1830.<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-28)</sup> The name "[Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth) of Australia" for the new federation of the six former colonies was formalised in the *[Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Australia)* (UK).[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-National_Library_of_Australia-2024-26)

Colloquial names for Australia include "Oz", "Straya" and "[Down Under](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down_Under)".[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-29)

## History

### Indigenous prehistory

[Indigenous Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_Australians) comprise two broad groups:

- [Aboriginal Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians), who are the various [Indigenous peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples) of the Australian mainland and many of its islands, including [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Tasmanians)
- [Torres Strait Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_Strait_Islanders), who are a distinct [Melanesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanesia) people of [Torres Strait Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_Strait_Islands)

Human habitation of the Australian continent is estimated to have begun 50,000 to 65,000 years ago,[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Veth-30)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Clarkson-2017-31)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Williams-2021-32)<sup>[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-33)</sup> with the migration of people by [land bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_bridge) and short sea crossings from what is now Southeast Asia.<sup>[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Veth-30)</sup> It is uncertain how many waves of immigration may have contributed to these ancestors of modern Aboriginal Australians.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Malaspinas-2016-34)<sup>[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-35)</sup> The [Madjedbebe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madjedbebe) rock shelter in [Arnhem Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnhem_Land) is possibly the oldest site showing the presence of humans in Australia.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Clarkson-2017-31)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Williams-2021-32)<sup>[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-36)</sup> The oldest human remains found are the [Lake Mungo remains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Mungo_remains), which have been dated to approximately 42,000 years ago.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-37)

Aboriginal Australian culture is one of the oldest continuous cultures on Earth.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-38)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-39)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-40)<sup>[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Malaspinas-2016-34)</sup> At the time of first European contact, Aboriginal Australians belonged to wide range of societies, with diverse economies spread across at least [250 different language groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Aboriginal_languages).[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-41)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-42)<sup>[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Flood_2019-2-23)</sup> Estimates of the Aboriginal population before British settlement range from 300,000 to 3 million.<sup>[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-43)</sup> Aboriginal Australians cultures were (and remain) deeply connected with the land and the environment, with stories of [The Dreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dreaming) maintained through [oral tradition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_tradition), [songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songline), dance and paintings.<sup>[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Mawson-2021-44)</sup> Certain groups engaged in [fire-stick farming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire-stick_farming),[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-45)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-46)[fish farming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_farming),[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-47)<sup>[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-48)</sup> and built [semi-permanent shelters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_architecture#Australia).<sup>[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-49)</sup> These practices have variously been characterised as "[hunter-gatherer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer)", "[agricultural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture)", "natural cultivation" and "intensification".[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Mawson-2021-44)[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-50)[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-51)[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Flood_2019-52)

Torres Strait Islander people first settled their islands at least 2,500 years ago.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Veth-2-53)<sup>[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-54)</sup> Culturally and linguistically distinct from mainland Aboriginal peoples, they were seafarers and obtained their livelihood from seasonal horticulture and the resources of their reefs and seas. Agriculture also developed on some islands and villages appeared by the 1300s.<sup>[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Veth-2-53)</sup> By the mid-18th century in northern Australia, [contact, trade and cross-cultural engagement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makassan_contact_with_Australia) had been established between local Aboriginal groups and [Makassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makassar_people) [trepangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trepanging), visiting from present-day Indonesia.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-55)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-56)[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-57)

### European exploration and colonisation

In 1606 the crew of the Dutch ship, *[Duyfken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duyfken)*, captained by [Willem Janszoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_Janszoon), made the first documented European landing in Australia and contact with Aboriginal Australians.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-58)</sup> Later that year, [Luís Vaz de Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luís_Vaz_de_Torres) sailed to the north of Australia through [Torres Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_Strait), along New Guinea's southern coast.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-59)[Abel Tasman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Tasman)'s voyage of 1642 was the first known European expedition to reach [Van Diemen's Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Diemen's_Land). On his second voyage of 1644, he mapped the north coast of Australia south of New Guinea. Following Tasman's voyages, the Dutch were able to make almost complete maps of Australia's northern and western coasts and much of its southern and south-eastern Tasmanian coasts. They named the continent [New Holland](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Holland_(Australia)>).[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-60)

In 1770, Captain [James Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cook) sailed along and mapped the east coast, which he named "[New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales)" and claimed for Great Britain.<sup>[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-61)</sup> In 1786, the British government announced its intention to establish a [penal colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penal_colony) in New South Wales.<sup>[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-62)</sup> On 26 January 1788, the [First Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Fleet) commanded by Captain [Arthur Phillip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Phillip), arrived at [Sydney Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Cove), Port Jackson. A camp was established and the [Union Flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Great_Britain) raised and the date later became [Australia's national day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Day).[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-63)

Most early settlers were [convicts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convicts_in_Australia), [transported](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penal_transportation) for petty crimes and [assigned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convict_assignment) as labourers or servants to "free settlers" (willing immigrants). Once [emancipated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipist), convicts tended to integrate into colonial society. Aboriginal resistance, convict rebellions and [bushranging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bushranger) were sometimes suppressed under martial law.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-64)<sup>[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-65)</sup> The 1808 [Rum Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rum_Rebellion), carried out by officers of the [New South Wales Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales_Corps), led to a temporary [military junta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_junta).<sup>[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-66)</sup> During the next two decades, social and economic reforms, together with the establishment of a [Legislative Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales_Legislative_Council) and [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_New_South_Wales), saw the penal colony transition to a civil society.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-67)

The indigenous population declined for 150 years following European settlement, mainly due to infectious disease.<sup>[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-68)</sup> British colonial authorities did not sign any treaties with [Aboriginal groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians#Groups_and_sub-groups).[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-69)<sup>[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-70)</sup> As settlement expanded, tens of thousands of Indigenous people and thousands of settlers were killed in [frontier conflicts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_frontier_wars), which many historians argue included acts of [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide_of_Indigenous_Australians) by settlers.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Reynolds_2022-71)<sup>[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-72)</sup> Settlers dispossessed surviving Indigenous peoples of most of their land.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Reynolds_2022-71)

### Colonial expansion

In 1803, a settlement was established in Van Diemen's Land (present-day [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania)),<sup>[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-73)</sup> and in 1813, [Gregory Blaxland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Blaxland), [William Lawson](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Lawson_(explorer)>) and [William Wentworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Wentworth) [crossed the Blue Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1813_crossing_of_the_Blue_Mountains) west of Sydney, opening the interior to European settlement.<sup>[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-74)</sup> The British claim was extended to the whole Australian continent in 1827 when Major [Edmund Lockyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Lockyer) established a settlement on [King George Sound](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_George_Sound_(Western_Australia)>) (modern-day [Albany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_Western_Australia)).<sup>[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-75)</sup> The [Swan River Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swan_River_Colony) (present-day [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth)) was established in 1829, evolving into the largest Australian colony by area, [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Western_Australia).<sup>[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-76)</sup> Separate colonies were carved from New South Wales: Tasmania in 1825, [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_colonisation_of_South_Australia) in 1836, [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Victoria) in 1851, and [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Queensland) in 1859.<sup>[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-77)</sup> South Australia and Victoria were founded as free colonies – they never accepted transported convicts.<sup>[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-78)</sup> Growing [opposition to the convict system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasian_Anti-Transportation_League) culminated in its abolition in the eastern colonies by the 1850s. Initially a free colony, Western Australia accepted convicts from 1850 to 1868.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-79)

The six colonies individually gained [responsible government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsible_government) between 1855 and 1890, managing most of their own affairs while remaining part of the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire).<sup>[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-80)</sup> The Colonial Office in London retained control of some matters, notably foreign affairs.<sup>[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-81)</sup> The colonial parliaments progressively extended voting rights to adult men from 1856, with [women's suffrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_suffrage) on equal terms following between the 1890s and 1900s. Some colonies introduced racial restrictions on voting from 1885.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-82)

In the mid-19th century, explorers such as [Burke and Wills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burke_and_Wills_expedition) charted Australia's interior.<sup>[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-83)</sup> A [series of gold rushes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_gold_rushes) beginning in the early 1850s led to an influx of new migrants from [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Australians), North America and continental Europe,<sup>[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-84)</sup> as well as outbreaks of [bushranging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bushranger) and civil unrest; the latter peaked in 1854 when [Ballarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballarat) miners launched the [Eureka Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eureka_Rebellion) against gold licence fees.<sup>[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-85)</sup> The 1860s saw the rise of [blackbirding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackbirding), where [South Sea Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sea_Islanders) were coerced or abducted into [indentured labour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indentured_labour), mainly by Queensland colonists.[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-86)[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-87)

From 1886, Australian colonial governments began [removing many Aboriginal children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stolen_Generations) from their families and communities, justified on the grounds of child protection and [forced assimilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_assimilation) policies.[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-88)[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-89)<sup>[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-90)</sup> The [Second Boer War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Boer_War) (1899–1902) marked the largest overseas deployment of [Australia's colonial forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_forces_of_Australia).[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-91)[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-92)

### Federation to the World Wars

On 1 January 1901, [federation of the colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia) was achieved after a decade of planning, [constitutional conventions](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Convention_(Australia)>) and [referendums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1898–1900_Australian_constitutional_referendums), resulting in the establishment of the Commonwealth of Australia as a nation under the new [Australian Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Australia).[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-93)

From 1901, Australia was a self-governing [dominion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion) within the British Empire.<sup>[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-94)</sup> It was one of the founding members of the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations) in 1920,<sup>[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-95)</sup> and the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_United_Nations) in 1945.<sup>[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-96)</sup> The *[Statute of Westminster 1931](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute_of_Westminster_1931)* ended the ability of the UK to legislate for Australia at the federal level without Australia's consent. Australia [adopted it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute_of_Westminster_Adoption_Act_1942) in 1942, but it was backdated to 1939 to confirm the validity of legislation passed during World War II.[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-97)

The [Australian Capital Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory) was formed in 1911 as the location for the future federal capital of [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra). While it was being constructed, [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne) served as the temporary capital from 1901 to 1927.<sup>[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-98)</sup> The [Northern Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Territory) was transferred from South Australia to the Commonwealth in 1911.<sup>[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-99)</sup> Australia took over the administration of the [Territory of Papua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Papua) (previously [British New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_New_Guinea)) in 1905 and of the [Territory of New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_New_Guinea) (formerly [German New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_New_Guinea)) in 1920. The two were unified as the [Territory of Papua and New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Papua_and_New_Guinea) in 1949 and gained independence from Australia in 1975.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-100)

In 1914, Australia joined the [Allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I) in the First World War, and took part in the fighting on several fronts.<sup>[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-101)</sup> Of the 324,000 men who served overseas, about 60,000 were killed and another 152,000 were wounded.<sup>[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-102)</sup> Many Australians regard the defeat of the [Australian and New Zealand Army Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_and_New_Zealand_Army_Corps) (ANZAC) at [Gallipoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallipoli_Campaign) in 1915 as the "baptism of fire" that forged the [new nation's identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anzac_spirit).[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Macintyre_2020-103)<sup>[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-104)</sup> The [beginning of the campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landing_at_Anzac_Cove) is commemorated annually on [Anzac Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anzac_Day), a date which rivals [Australia Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Day) as the nation's most important.[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Macintyre_2020-103)[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-105)

From 1939 to 1945, Australia joined the [Allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II) in fighting the Second World War. Australia's [armed forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Defence_Force) fought in the [Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War), [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Theatre_of_World_War_II) and [Mediterranean and Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_and_Middle_East_theatre_of_World_War_II) [theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_theaters_and_campaigns_of_World_War_II).<sup>[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-106)</sup> The shock of Britain's [defeat in Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Singapore) in 1942, followed soon after by the [bombing of Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombing_of_Darwin) and [other Japanese attacks on Australian soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_raids_on_Australia,_1942–43), led to a widespread belief in Australia that [a Japanese invasion was imminent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposed_Japanese_invasion_of_Australia_during_World_War_II), and a shift from the United Kingdom to the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia–United_States_relations) as Australia's principal ally and security partner.<sup>[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-107)</sup> Since 1951, Australia has maintained a mutual security alliance with the United States under the [ANZUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANZUS) treaty.[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-108)

### Post-war and contemporary eras

In the three decades following World War II, Australia experienced significant increases in living standards, leisure time and suburban development.<sup>[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-109)</sup> Governments encouraged a [large wave of immigration from across Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-war_immigration_to_Australia) and called these migrants "[New Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Australians)". High immigration was justified to Australians using the slogan "populate or perish",<sup>[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-110)</sup> and from the 1960s the [White Australia policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Australia_policy) was gradually relaxed.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-111)

A member of the [Western Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Bloc) during the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War), Australia participated in the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_in_the_Korean_War) and the [Malayan Emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Australia_during_the_Malayan_Emergency) during the 1950s and the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Australia_during_the_Vietnam_War) from 1962 to 1973.[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-112)<sup>[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-113)</sup> Tensions over communist influence in society led to [unsuccessful attempts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1951_Australian_Communist_Party_ban_referendum) by the [Menzies Government](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menzies_Government_(1949–1966)>) to ban the [Communist Party of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Australia), and a [bitter split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party_split_of_1955) in the [Labor Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party) in 1955.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-114)

As a result of a [1967 referendum](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_referendum,_1967_(Aboriginals)>), the federal government gained the power to legislate with regard to Aboriginal Australians, and Aboriginal Australians were fully included in the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_in_Australia).[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-115)[Pre-colonial land interests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_title) (referred to as [native title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_title_in_Australia) in Australia) were recognised in law for the first time when the [High Court of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Australia) held in *[Mabo v Queensland (No 2)](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mabo_v_Queensland_(No_2)>)* that Australia was not *[terra nullius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_nullius)* ('land belonging to no one') at the time of European settlement.[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-116)[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-117)[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-118)

Following the abolition of the last vestiges of the [White Australia policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Australia_policy) in 1973,<sup>[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-119)</sup> Australia's demography and culture transformed as a result of a large and ongoing wave of non-European immigration, mostly from Asia.<sup>[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-120)</sup> During the late 20th century, Australia increased its foreign policy ties within the [Asia–Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia–Pacific) region.<sup>[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-121)</sup> The [Australia Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Acts) of 1986 severed the remaining constitutional ties between Australia and the United Kingdom while maintaining the monarch in her independent capacity as [Queen of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_Australia).[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-122)<sup>[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-123)</sup> In a [1999 constitutional referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Australian_republic_referendum), 55% of voters rejected [abolishing the monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_Australia) and becoming a republic.[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-124)

Following the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks) in the United States, Australia joined the United States in fighting the [Afghanistan War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Australia_during_the_War_in_Afghanistan) from 2001 to 2021 and the [Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_contribution_to_the_2003_invasion_of_Iraq) from 2003 to 2009.<sup>[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-125)</sup> The nation's trade relations also became increasingly oriented towards East Asia in the 21st century, with China becoming the nation's [largest trading partner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_largest_trading_partners_of_Australia) by a large margin.[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-126)

In response to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Australia), from March 2020 [lockdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns) and other restrictions on public gatherings and movement across the national and state borders were implemented by the Federal, state and territory governments. Following the rollout of vaccines in 2021, these restrictions were gradually eased. In October 2023, Australia declared that COVID-19 was no longer a communicable disease incident of national significance.[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-127)

## Geography

### General characteristics

Australia consists of the mainland Australian continent, the island of Tasmania, numerous smaller offshore islands, and the remote offshore territories of [Ashmore and Cartier Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashmore_and_Cartier_Islands), [Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Island), [Cocos (Keeling) Islands](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocos_(Keeling)_Islands>), [Coral Sea Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Sea_Islands), [Heard and McDonald Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heard_Island_and_McDonald_Islands), and [Norfolk Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Island).<sup>[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-128)</sup> Australia also claims about 42% of Antarctica as the [Australian Antarctic Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Antarctic_Territory), but this claim is only recognised by four other countries.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Scott_2021-21)

Mainland Australia lies between latitudes [9°](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_parallel_south) and [44° south](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/44th_parallel_south), and longitudes [112°](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/112th_meridian_east) and [154° east](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/154th_meridian_east).<sup>[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Geoscience_Australia-2014a-12)</sup> Surrounded by the Indian and Pacific oceans, Australia is separated from Asia by the [Arafura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arafura_Sea) and [Timor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timor_Sea) seas, with the [Coral Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Sea) lying off the Queensland coast, and the [Tasman Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasman_Sea) lying between Australia and New Zealand. The [Great Barrier Reef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Barrier_Reef), the world's largest coral reef, lies a short distance off the north-east coast and extends for more than 2,300 km (1,400 mi).[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-129)

The mainland is the world's smallest continent and the country is the [sixth-largest by total area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_outlying_territories_by_total_area).<sup>[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Blewett_2012-130)</sup> Australia is sometimes considered the world's [largest island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_by_area)<sup>[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-131)</sup> and is often dubbed the "island continent".<sup>[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-132)</sup> It has 35,877 km (22,293 mi) of coastline (excluding all offshore islands),<sup>[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Blewett_2012-130)</sup> and claims an [exclusive economic zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone_of_Australia) of 8,148,250 square kilometres (3,146,060 sq mi). This exclusive economic zone does not include the [Australian Antarctic Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Antarctic_Territory).[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-133)

About 70% of Australia's landmass is arid or semi-arid.<sup>[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Blewett_2012-3-134)</sup> In 2021, Australia had 10% of the global permanent meadows and pastureland.[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-135)[Forest cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_cover) is about 17% of Australia's land area.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-136)<sup>[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-137)</sup> The Australian mainland is relatively flat, with an average height of 325 metres (1,066 ft) compared with 870 metres (2,850 ft) for all continents.<sup>[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-138)</sup> The [Great Dividing Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Dividing_Range) runs along most of eastern Australia, dividing the central lowlands from the eastern highlands.<sup>[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Geoscience_Australia-2014-139)</sup> At 2,228 m (7,310 ft), [Mount Kosciuszko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kosciuszko) is the highest mountain on the mainland. Taller are [Mawson Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mawson_Peak), at 2,745 m (9,006 ft), on Heard Island, and, in the Australian Antarctic Territory, [Mount McClintock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_McClintock) and [Mount Menzies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Menzies), at 3,492 m (11,457 ft) and 3,355 m (11,007 ft) respectively.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Geoscience_Australia-2014-139)

The [Murray-Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray–Darling_basin) is Australia's major river system, draining most of inland New South Wales and Southern Queensland towards [Lake Alexandrina](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Alexandrina_(South_Australia)>) and the sea in South Australia. There are also smaller coastal river systems, inland drainage systems such as the [Lake Eyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Eyre_basin) system, and salt lake systems in central and western Australia.<sup>[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-140)</sup> Australia's rivers have the lowest discharge into the sea of any continent. The mainland's flat, arid profile also makes its rivers slow-moving, resulting in a build up of salt on the land.<sup>[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-141)</sup> Salinisation adversely affects Australia's soil which is, on average, poor in nutrients compared with world standards.[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-142)

Australia's population is concentrated on the coastal fringes. About 95% of the population lives within 100 km of the coast; the world average is 39%.<sup>[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Blewett_2012-2-143)</sup> Australia's [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density) is 3.5 inhabitants per square kilometre,<sup>[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Australian_Bureau_of_Statistics-2023-24)</sup> which is one of the lowest in the world.<sup>[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Blewett_2012-2-143)</sup> However, there is a large concentration of the population in cities along the temperate south-eastern coastline, and population density exceeds 38 inhabitants per square kilometre in central Melbourne.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Australian_Bureau_of_Statistics-2023-24)

### Geology

Formerly part of the [Rodinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodinia) and [Gondwana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondwana) [supercontinents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercontinent),<sup>[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-144)</sup> Australia completely separated from Antarctica about 35 million years ago and continued drifting northwards.<sup>[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-145)</sup> When the [Last Glacial Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Glacial_Period) ended, rising sea levels separated the Australian mainland from New Guinea about 8,000 years ago and from [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania) about 6,000 years ago.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-145)

Australia lies well within the [Australian tectonic plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_plate). The mainland is relatively stable geologically, with no major mountain building, active volcanoes or tectonic faults.<sup>[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-146)</sup> However, the Australian plate is moving north-northeast at a rate of about 6 to 7 cm a year and is in collision with the [Eurasian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurasian_plate) and [Pacific plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_plate).<sup>[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-2-147)</sup> The resulting intratectonic stresses lead to relatively high seismic activity for a geologically stable landmass. There were 18 earthquakes with a [moment magnitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale) of greater than 6 between 1901 and 2017.<sup>[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-2-147)</sup> The [Newcastle earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Newcastle_earthquake) of 1989 was Australia's deadliest, killing 13 people.<sup>[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-148)</sup> There were active volcanoes on the eastern mainland as recently as 4,600 years ago,<sup>[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-3-149)</sup> and this is reflected in Aboriginal place names and creation stories.<sup>[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-150)</sup> Currently, [volcanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanism) occurs in the remote [Heard Island and McDonald Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heard_Island_and_McDonald_Islands).[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-151)

The Australian continental crust was created in three cycles from the oldest [Archaean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archean) [cratons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craton) in the west to the younger [orogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orogenic_belt) formations in the east (built about 541 million to 252 million years ago).[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-3-149)<sup>[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-152)</sup> The oldest Australian surface rocks date to the Archaean period. Some in Western Australia are older than 3.7 billion years and others in South Australia are over 3.1 billion years old. The oldest zircon crystals on Earth, dating back 4.4 billion years, have been found in Western Australia. However, about 80% of Australia is covered by sedimentary rocks and [regolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regolith) that are less than 250 million years old.[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Kennett-3-149)

### Climate

The Australian climate ranges from wet tropical in the northeast and northwest to arid in the centre. The coastal south is temperate and humid with winter freezing and snow in the southeastern highlands and Tasmania.

The **Australian Capital Territory** (**ACT**), known as the **Federal Capital Territory** until 1938, is an internal [territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_Australia) of Australia. [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra), the capital city of Australia, is situated within the territory and is the territory's [primate city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primate_city). The Australian Capital Territory is located in southeastern Australia as an [enclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave_and_exclave) surrounded by the state of [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales). The territory was excised from New South Wales in 1911 to serve as the [seat of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seat_of_government) for the Commonwealth, in accordance with Section 125 of the [Australian Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Australia). Today, the ACT hosts important institutions, such as the [Parliament of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Australia) and [High Court of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Australia), as well as the headquarters of many [federal departments and agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Australian_Government_entities).

On 1 January 1901, the self-governing Australian colonies [federated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia) to form the Commonwealth of Australia. Section 125 of the [Australian Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Australia) provided that a tract of land, situated in New South Wales and not less than 100 miles (160 km) from [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney), would be ceded to the new [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Australia). Following discussion and exploration of various sites within New South Wales, the *[Seat of Government Act 1908](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seat_of_Government_Act_1908)* was passed in 1908, and specified a capital in the Yass-Canberra region. The territory was transferred to the federal government by [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales) on 1 January 1911, and on 12 March 1913, the city of Canberra was officially proclaimed as the nation’s capital.

Whilst the overwhelming majority of the territory’s population resides in the city of [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra) in the territory's north-east, the territory also includes smaller towns such as [Williamsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsdale,_Australian_Capital_Territory), [Oaks Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oaks_Estate,_Australian_Capital_Territory), [Uriarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uriarra,_Australian_Capital_Territory), [Tharwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tharwa,_Australian_Capital_Territory) and [Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall,_Australian_Capital_Territory). The territory also includes the [Namadgi National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namadgi_National_Park), which comprises the majority of land within the territory. Although a common misconception, the [Jervis Bay Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jervis_Bay_Territory) is not part of the ACT; however, ACT laws apply in the Jervis Bay Territory.<sup>[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:1-23)</sup> The territory has a relatively dry, continental climate, experiencing warm to hot summers and cool to cold winters. Among the [states and territories of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_Australia), the Australian Capital Territory is the only one that is geographically [landlocked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked).

The territory is home to important political and governing institutions, as well as many monuments and museums. These include, but are not limited to, the [Parliament of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Australia), [High Court of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Australia), [Royal Australian Mint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Australian_Mint), [National Gallery of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Gallery_of_Australia), [National Museum of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Australia), [National Library of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_Australia), [Royal Military College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Military_College,_Duntroon), [Australian Defence Force Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Defence_Force_Academy), and the [Australian War Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_War_Memorial). It also hosts the majority of foreign embassies in Australia, as well as regional headquarters of many international organisations, not-for-profits, lobbying groups and professional associations. Several major universities also have campuses in the territory, including the [Australian National University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_National_University), the [University of Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Canberra), the [University of New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_South_Wales), [Charles Sturt University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Sturt_University) and the [Australian Catholic University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Catholic_University).

A locally elected [legislative assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory_Legislative_Assembly) has governed the territory since 1988. However, the Commonwealth maintains authority over the territory and may disallow or overturn local laws. The Commonwealth maintains control over the area known as the [Parliamentary Triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_Triangle,_Canberra) through the [National Capital Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Authority). Residents of the territory, together with residents of the [Jervis Bay Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jervis_Bay_Territory) and [Norfolk Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Island), elect three members of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_House_of_Representatives) and two [senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Senate). While senators who represent Australian states have fixed six-year terms, the terms of territory senators are not fixed, but rather are governed by the opening and dissolution of the House of Representatives.

With 475,600 residents, the territory is the second-smallest mainland state or territory by population. At the [2016 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Australian_census), the median weekly income for people in the territory aged over 15 was $998, significantly higher than the national median of $662.<sup>[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-census-24)</sup> The average level of degree qualification in the territory is also higher than the national average. Within the territory, 37.1% of the population hold a bachelor's degree or higher, compared to the national figure of 20%.<sup>[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-census-24)</sup> The ACT also has high standards of living: in 2023, the territory recorded the second-highest subnational [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index) (HDI) score of 0.988 [out of over 1,700](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_subnational_entities_with_the_highest_and_lowest_Human_Development_Index) in the world, just below [Zurich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zurich).

[Indigenous Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians) have long inhabited the area.<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)</sup> Evidence indicates habitation dating back at least 25,000 years,<sup>[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-26)</sup> and it is possible that the area was inhabited for considerably longer. The principal group occupying the region were the [Ngunnawal people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngunnawal), with the [Ngarigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngarigo) and [Walgalu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walgalu) living immediately to the south, the [Wandadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wandandian) to the east, the [Gandangara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandangara) to the north and the [Wiradjuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiradjuri) to the north-west.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Gillespie84-27)

Following European settlement, the growth of the new colony of New South Wales led to an increasing demand for [arable land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arable_land).<sup>[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Gillespie84-27)</sup> Governor [Lachlan Macquarie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lachlan_Macquarie) supported expeditions to open up new lands to the south of [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney).<sup>[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-28)</sup> The 1820s saw further exploration in the Canberra area associated with the construction of a road from Sydney to the [Goulburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goulburn) plains. While working on the project, [Charles Throsby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Throsby) learned of a nearby lake and river from the local Indigenous peoples and he accordingly sent Wild to lead a small party to investigate the site. The search was unsuccessful, but they did discover the [Yass River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yass_River), and it is surmised that they would have set foot on part of the future territory.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:4-29)

A second expedition was mounted shortly thereafter, and they became the first Europeans to camp at the [Molonglo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molonglo_River) and [Queanbeyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queanbeyan_River) Rivers.<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)</sup> However, they failed to find the [Murrumbidgee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrumbidgee_River).<sup>[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:4-29)</sup> The issue of the Murrumbidgee was solved in 1821 when Throsby mounted a third expedition and successfully reached the watercourse, on the way providing the first detailed account of the land that now comprises the territory.<sup>[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:4-29)</sup> The last expedition in the region before settlement was undertaken by [Allan Cunningham](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Cunningham_(botanist)>) in 1824.<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)</sup> He reported that the region was suitable for grazing and the settlement of the Limestone Plains followed immediately thereafter.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-30)

The first land grant in the region was made to Joshua John Moore in 1823, and European settlement in the area began in 1824 with the construction of a homestead by his stockmen on what is now the [Acton Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acton_Peninsula).<sup>[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-28)</sup> Moore formally purchased the site in 1826 and named the property *Canberry* or *Canberra*.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)

A significant influx of population and economic activity occurred around the 1850s [gold rushes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_gold_rushes).<sup>[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-31)</sup> The gold rushes prompted the establishment of communication between Sydney and the region by way of the [Cobb & Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobb_and_Co) coaches, which transported mail and passengers.<sup>[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:5-32)</sup> The first post offices opened in [Ginninderra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginninderra) in 1859 and at Lanyon in 1860.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-28)

During colonial times, the European communities of Ginninderra, [Molonglo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molonglo_Plains) and Tuggeranong settled and farmed the surrounding land. The region was also called the [Queanbeyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queanbeyan)-[Yass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yass,_New_South_Wales) district, after the two largest towns in the area. The villages of Ginninderra and Tharwa developed to service the local agrarian communities.

During the first 20 years of settlement, there was only limited contact between the settlers and Aboriginal people. Over the succeeding years, the Ngunnawal and other local indigenous people effectively ceased to exist as cohesive and independent communities adhering to their traditional ways of life.<sup>[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-28)</sup> Those who had not succumbed to disease and other predations either dispersed to the local settlements or were relocated to more distant [Aboriginal reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_reserve) set up by the New South Wales government in the latter part of the 19th century.<sup>\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)*\]</sup>

In 1898, a referendum on a proposed constitution was held in four of the colonies – [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales), [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia), [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania), and [Victoria](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia)>). Although the referendum achieved a majority in all four colonies, the New South Wales referendum failed to gain the minimum number of votes needed for the bill to pass. Following this result, a meeting of the four premiers in 1898 heard from [George Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Reid), the [Premier of New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_New_South_Wales), who argued that locating the future capital in New South Wales would be sufficient to ensure the passage of the bill. The 1899 referendum on this revised bill was successful and passed with sufficient numbers.<sup>[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-33)</sup> Section 125 of the [Australian Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Australia) thus provided that, following Federation in 1901, land would be ceded freely to the new [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Government).<sup>\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)*\]</sup>

This, however, left open the question of where to locate the capital. In 1906 and after significant deliberations, New South Wales agreed to cede sufficient land on the condition that it was in the [Yass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yass,_New_South_Wales)-[Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra) region,<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)</sup> this site being closer to Sydney.<sup>[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-ausmap-34)</sup> Initially, [Dalgety, New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalgety,_New_South_Wales) remained at the forefront, but Yass-Canberra prevailed after voting by federal representatives.<sup>[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:4-29)</sup> The *[Seat of Government Act 1908](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seat_of_Government_Act_1908)* was passed in 1908, which repealed the 1904 Act and specified a capital in the Yass-Canberra region.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)<sup>[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-35)</sup> Government surveyor [Charles Scrivener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Scrivener) was deployed to the region in the same year to map out a specific site and, after an extensive search, settled upon the present location,<sup>[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-36)</sup> basing the borders primarily on the need to secure a stable water supply for the planned capital.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-37)

The territory was transferred to the Commonwealth by [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales) on 1 January 1911, two years before the naming of Canberra as the national capital on 20 March 1913.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-39)

The Commonwealth gained control of all land within the borders of the new territory but ownership only of NSW Crown land, with significant parcels of extant freehold remaining in the hands of their pre-existing owners. Much of this was acquired during [World War One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_One), though a few titles were not transferred until the late 20th century.

Land within the territory is granted under a [leasehold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leasehold) system, with [99-year residential leases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/99-year_lease) sold to buyers as new suburbs are planned, surveyed, and developed. The current policy is for these leases to be extended for another 99-year period on expiry, subject to payment of an administrative fee.<sup>[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-40)</sup> In an arrangement inspired by [Georgism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgism), the ideas of 19th-century American economist [Henry George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_George), leaseholders had to pay 5% of the unimproved value of the underlying land in rent until the [Gorton government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorton_government) abolished it in 1970.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-41)

In 1911, an international competition to design the future capital was held; it was won by the Chicago architect [Walter Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Burley_Griffin) in 1912.<sup>[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-28)</sup> The official naming of Canberra occurred on 12 March 1913 and construction began immediately.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-28)

After Griffin's departure following difficulty in implementing his project,<sup>[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-act-42)</sup> the [Federal Capital Advisory Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Capital_Advisory_Committee) was established in 1920 to advise the government of the construction efforts.<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)</sup> The committee had limited success meeting its goals. However, the chairman, [John Sulman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sulman), was instrumental in applying the ideas of the [garden city movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_city_movement) to Griffin's plan. The committee was replaced in 1925 by the [Federal Capital Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Capital_Commission).[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-25)

In 1930, the ACT Advisory Council was established to advise the minister for territories on the community's concerns. In 1934, the [Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Australian_Capital_Territory) was established.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-43)

From 1938 to 1957, the [National Capital Planning and Development Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Planning_and_Development_Committee) continued to plan the further expansion of Canberra. However, it did not have executive power, and decisions were made on the development of Canberra without consulting the committee.<sup>[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:5-32)</sup> During this time, Prime Minister [Robert Menzies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Menzies) regarded the state of the national capital as an embarrassment.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:6-44)

After World War II, there was a shortage of housing and office space in Canberra.<sup>[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-45)</sup> A Senate Select Committee hearing was held in 1954 to address its development requirements. This Committee recommended the creation of a single planning body with executive power. Consequently, the [National Capital Planning and Development Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Planning_and_Development_Committee) was replaced by the [National Capital Development Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Development_Commission) in 1957.<sup>[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-46)</sup> The [National Capital Development Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Development_Commission) ended four decades of disputes over the shape and design of [Lake Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Burley_Griffin) and construction was completed in 1964 after four years of work. The completion of the centrepiece of Griffin's design finally laid the platform for the development of Griffin's [Parliamentary Triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_Triangle,_Canberra).[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:6-44)

In 1978, an [advisory referendum was held](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Australian_Capital_Territory_self-government_referendum) to determine the views of citizens resident in the territory about whether there should be self-government. Just under 64 percent of voters rejected devolved government options, in favour of the status quo.<sup>[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-47)</sup> Nevertheless, in 1988, the new federal minister for the territory [Gary Punch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Punch) received a report recommending the abolition of the [National Capital Development Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Development_Commission) and the formation of a locally elected government. Punch recommended that the [Hawke government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hawke) accept the report's recommendations and subsequently [Clyde Holding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Holding) introduced legislation to grant self-government to the territory in October 1988.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-48)

The enactment on 6 December 1988 of the *[Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Act 1988](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory_(Self-Government)_Act_1988>)* established the framework for self-government.<sup>[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-ACT1988-49)</sup> The [first election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Australian_Capital_Territory_election) for the 17-member [Australian Capital Territory Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory_Legislative_Assembly) was held on 4 March 1989.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-50)

The initial years of self-government were difficult and unstable.<sup>[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-anniv-51)</sup> A majority of territory residents had opposed self-government and had it imposed upon them by the federal parliament. At the first election, 4 of the 17 seats were won by anti-self-government single-issue parties due to a protest vote by disgruntled Canberrans and a total of 8 were won by minor parties and independents.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-anniv-51)

In 1992, Labor won eight seats and the minor parties and independents won only three. Stability increased, and in 1995, [Kate Carnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Carnell) became the first elected Liberal chief minister. In 1998, Carnell became the first chief minister to be re-elected.

The territory is 2,358 km<sup>2</sup> (910 mi<sup>2</sup>) in area, slightly smaller than Luxembourg.

It is bounded by the [Bombala railway line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombala_railway_line) in the east, the [watershed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_divide) of [Naas Creek](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naas_(valley)>) in the south, the watershed of the [Cotter River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotter_River) in the west and the watershed of the [Molonglo River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molonglo_River) in the north-east. These boundaries were set to give the territory an adequate water supply.<sup>[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-52)</sup> The territory extends about 88.5 km (55.0 mi) north-south between 35.124°S and 35.921°S, and 57.75 km (35.88 mi) west-east between 148.763°E and 149.399°E.<sup>[\[note 1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-53)</sup> The city area of [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra) occupies the north-eastern corner of this area.

The territory includes the city of [Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra) and some towns such as [Williamsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsdale,_Australian_Capital_Territory), [Oaks Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oaks_Estate), [Uriarra Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uriarra_Village), [Tharwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tharwa) and [Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall,_Australian_Capital_Territory). The territory also contains agricultural land ([sheep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_sheep), [dairy cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dairy_cattle), [vineyards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vineyard) and small amounts of crops) and a large area of national park ([Namadgi National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namadgi_National_Park)), much of it mountainous and forested.

Tidbinbilla is a locality to the south-west of Canberra that features the [Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidbinbilla_Nature_Reserve) and the [Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Deep_Space_Communication_Complex), operated by the United States' [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA) as part of its [Deep Space Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_Space_Network). The [Southern Tablelands Temperate Grassland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Tablelands_Temperate_Grassland) straddles the state.

The territory includes a large range of mountains, rivers and creeks, largely contained within the [Namadgi National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namadgi_National_Park). These include the Naas and Murrumbidgee Rivers.

In September 2022, a proposal was announced to change the border between NSW and the territory, the first change since the territory was created in 1911.<sup>[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-54)</sup> ACT chief minister [Andrew Barr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Barr) said NSW premier [Dominic Perrottet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Perrottet) had agreed to a proposed border change of 330 ha (1.3 sq mi) in the [Ginninderra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginninderra) watershed.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-55)

The territory has a relatively dry, continental climate, experiencing warm to hot summers and cool to cold winters.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> Under the [Köppen-Geiger classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Köppen-Geiger_climate_classification_system), the territory has an [oceanic climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate) (*Cfb*).[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-57)

January is the hottest month with an average high of 27.7 °C.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> July is the coldest month when the average high drops to 11.2 °C (52.2 °F).<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> The highest maximum temperature recorded in the territory was 44.0 °C on 4 January 2020. The lowest minimum temperature was −10.0 °C on 11 July 1971.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)

Rainfall varies significantly across the territory.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> Much higher rainfall occurs in the mountains to the west of Canberra compared to the east.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> The mountains act as a barrier during winter with the city receiving less rainfall.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> Average annual rainfall in the territory is 629mm and there is an average of 108 rain days annually.<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)</sup> The wettest month is October, with an average rainfall of 65.3mm, and the driest month is June, with an average of 39.6mm.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)

Frost is common in the winter months. [Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow_in_Australia) is rare in Canberra's city centre, but the surrounding areas get annual snowfall through winter and often the snow-capped mountains can be seen from the city. The last significant snowfall in the city centre was in 1968.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-56)

Smoke haze became synonymous with the 2019/2020 Australian summer. On 1 January 2020 Canberra had the worst air quality of any major city in the world, with an AQI of 7700 (USAQI 949).[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-58)
